items.t: At 19, founder raises $11M for Ghost, maker of a $3,499 computer for personal AI
items.d: Ghost announced Monday its official emergence from stealth and an $11 million seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz.
items.fullText: For much of his life, Zain Javaid, 19, wanted to be a quant who uses math and data to guide his investment decisions. And for a while, he was one. But he got bored. Then, in 2022, ChatGPT was released, and he told TechCrunch, “I felt fundamentally excited in a way that I never had been before.” He became interested in personal AI, and that interest led him to start Ghost, which announced Monday that it has emerged from stealth after a year of building, along with an $11 million seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz. Other investors in the round include Abstract, Audacious Ventures, SV Angel, and Nova. His founding team includes Nicholas Chua, 19, Yifei Chen, 24, and Gautam Sharda, 23. Ghost’s first product is Core, a personal computer designed specifically for AI agents that can take actions on a person’s behalf. According to Javaid, the idea is to centralize a person’s data, from what’s on their desktop to apps to smart home devices, into one piece of hardware designed to continuously run AI agents that can act as an assistant, perform tasks, and understand a person’s life. “You can run models on existing hardware, but it’s a terrible experience on many levels,” said Javaid, who is also Core’s CEO. Image Credits: Ghost Core includes an Nvidia RTX Pro 4000 SFF Blackwell GPU (a type of chip commonly used to run AI models), said Javaid, adding that the GPU is bundled into the device’s price, so customers don’t need to buy one separately. He said it also has its own software layer, browser, and filing system and can continuously process information and tasks without constant prompting. Core costs $3,499. Preorders for the first batch open Monday, and shipping is scheduled for the last week of October. Javaid described Core as a “brain in a box” without a screen, which users access through a phone or app. Voice mode is also available, but users must speak into the Core app rather than the box

items.t: Hackers steal 8 million citizens’ records from Danish government database
items.d: The Danish government said the breach of names, addresses, and state-issued ID numbers affects 8 million people, including people living abroad and the deceased.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 7:58 AM PDT · October 5, 2026 Image Credits: Kristian Tuxen Ladegaard Berg / NurPhoto / Getty Images Zack Whittaker Hackers steal 8 million citizens’ records from Danish government database The Danish government has confirmed that its central database of citizens’ data was breached and most of its contents were stolen. The data breach affects some 8 million citizens and residents of Denmark, including people living abroad and the deceased. In a statement, Danish minister Christina Egelund said the breach of the country’s Central Person Register (CPR) was a “serious incident,” which allowed hackers to steal names, addresses, Danish social security numbers, and other information. The CPR is a government database of Danish citizens’ information, including their government-issued identity number for paying taxes and accessing other services. Denmark’s current population is about 6 million people, but the database includes records for about 11 million people, with some of the data going back decades. The Danish government would not say who is behind the breach, which happened in September but was discovered on October 2. However, it said the unauthorized access was obtained by “abusing a Danish company’s lawful access to search for information in the CPR system.” (Some companies in Denmark have access to the CPR for verifying people’s information with the government.) The data breach is thought to be the biggest in the country’s history. It follows similar cyberattacks targeting government national identity databases, including a 2016 breach affecting millions of Turkish citizens and several exposures of national ID cards and data spilled from India’s national Aadhaar database of citizens. items.t: Global tech policymakers agree to embrace AI in science
items.d: A joint statement issued by the U.S. and 15 other countries touts the technology’s potential to accelerate scientific progress.
items.fullText: EXCLUSIVE Artificial intelligence Artificial intelligence Global tech policymakers agree to embrace AI in science A joint statement issued by the U.S. and 15 other countries touts the technology’s potential to accelerate scientific progress. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 President Donald Trump speaks in the East Room of the White House on Tuesday during a lunch meeting with top executives of AI firms as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, left, and Elon Musk listen. Jacquelyn Martin / AP Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 3, 2026, 9:00 AM EDT By Jared Perlo The United States on Sunday will release a joint statement with 15 other countries describing a shared vision for a “golden age of science” that embraces the potential of artificial intelligence. The announcement is expected in Kyoto, Japan, at this year’s Science and Technology in Society Forum, an annual gathering of experts and policymakers that began in 2004. The statement, titled the “Kyoto Vision for a Golden Age of Science,” begins by recognizing science and technology’s benefits to society then goes on to encourage research that integrates artificial intelligence. (The statement calls it “super intelligence,” given President Donald Trump’s recent executive order renaming the technology.) “Super Intelligence and new ways of organizing research are opening entirely new frontiers of discovery,” reads the statement, which was seen by NBC News. “We recognize the opportunity to take advantage of these changes.” Michael Kratsios, head of the White House’s Office of Science and Technology Policy, spearheaded the vision statement, which also says the participating countries welcome the “growing field of metascience,” a term that describes the study of the scientific process itself. Tech ministers from Japan, Korea, the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates were among the representatives from other countries that endorsed the statement. Senate Democrats block Husted-led bill on data centers, calling it ‘toothless’
items.d: The bill aims to prevent data centers from spiking local utility costs. Republicans accused Democrats of playing political games, noting the bill passed the House 417-3.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Senate Democrats block Husted-led bill on data centers, calling it ‘toothless’ The bill aims to prevent data centers from spiking local utility costs. Republicans accused Democrats of playing political games, noting the bill passed the House 417-3. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio. Kevin Dietsch / Getty Images file Share Add NBC News to Google Sept. 30, 2026, 1:41 PM EDT By Sahil Kapur WASHINGTON — Senate Democrats blocked legislation Wednesday aimed at protecting consumers from paying higher prices when new data centers are built in their communities. The vote was 57-43, short of the 60 needed to break a filibuster. The Ratepayer Protection Act , which passed the House by a vote of 417-3 two weeks ago, would set a federal standard on the issue. It would also instruct state public utility commissions to find ways to make developers of data centers that use huge amounts of energy cover their own costs of water and electricity to consumers. The Senate version is led by appointed Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, who’s locked in a competitive battle as he seeks his first full Senate term. He is facing heat at home from Democratic rival Sherrod Brown, a former senator who has branded him “the face of data centers” for promoting developments when he was lieutenant governor. “I heard they said they wanted lower electricity prices,” Husted said of Democrats on Tuesday. “All they have to do is not block it, vote for it, and it will be on the president’s desk, and we will have a bipartisan win.” Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., said the bill would be merely “optional” for states and wouldn’t achieve much beyond partisan messaging for Republicans. “Plain and simple, the Ratepayer Protection Act is a fraud,” Schumer told reporters Tuesday. “It does not require any protections at all. While Americans are demanding real guardrails on AI and data centers, Republicans are offering a toothless messaging bill.

items.fullText: 판타지의 경계를 확장하다: 삼성 스페이셜 사이니지가 도쿄게임쇼 2026에서 펼치는 캐릭터 IP와 리테일의 미래 2026/09/23 AI 요약 새로운 뉴스룸 AI 기능을 살펴보세요! 닫기 --> AUDIO Play Download 공유 레이어 열기 인쇄하기 9월 17일부터 20일까지 일본 지바현 마쿠하리 멧세(Makuhari Messe)에서 열린 도쿄게임쇼 2026(Tokyo Game Show 2026, TGS). 글로벌 게임 기업 엔씨 부스는 게임 속 캐릭터를 눈앞에서 만나는 듯한 경험을 하려는 관람객들의 발길이 이어졌다. 그 중심에는 게임의 세계관을 화면 밖으로 확장한 삼성전자의 무안경 3D 디스플레이 ‘스페이셜 사이니지(Spatial Signage)’가 있었다. 이번 행사에서 엔씨가 선보인 ‘아스트라에 오라티오(Astrae Oratio)’는 마법이 일상에 스며든 판타지 세계를 배경으로 한 신전기 서브컬처 RPG다. 삼성 스페이셜 사이니지는 독자적인 ‘3D 플레이트(3D Plate)’ 기술을 적용해 별도의 3D 안경 없이도 콘텐츠에 생생한 입체감을 선사하며, 게임 속 캐릭터와 세계관을 오프라인 전시 공간으로 확장했다. 팬덤 경험 확장… 캐릭터와의 만남을 현실 공간으로 게임 퍼블리셔와 콘텐츠 IP(Intellectual Property, 지식재산권) 보유 기업에게 오프라인 공간은 디지털 콘텐츠를 현실로 가져오는 중요한 접점이다. 엔씨는 도쿄게임쇼에서 85형과 32형 스페이셜 사이니지를 부스 입구와 대기 공간 등에 배치해 관람객이 이동하는 과정에서도 게임 속 캐릭터와 세계관을 자연스럽게 경험하도록 했다. 부스 입구에는 85형 스페이셜 사이니지로 ‘아스트라에 오라티오’ 게임의 주요 배경인 ‘특구청’ 건물 내 엘리베이터를 재현했다. 대형 디스플레이를 통해 캐릭터를 실제 사람과 가까운 크기로 표현해, 마치 게임 속 등장인물들이 현실 세계에 인사를 건네는 듯한 장면을 연출했다. ▲ ‘아스트라에 오라티오’ 부스 입구에 설치한 85형 스페이셜 사이니지는 게임 속 다양한 캐릭터가 눈 앞으로 다가오는 듯한 연출로 관람객의 이목을 끌었다. 엔씨 아스트라에 오라티오 사업실 이용수 실장은 “관람객들이 부스에 들어서는 순간부터 실제 크기의 캐릭터와 마주하고 게임 세계에 몰입하길 바랐다”면서 “서브컬처 장르에서는 캐릭터의 생동감과 현실감이 특히 중요한데, 스페이셜 사이니지가 이런 특성을 관람객에게 효과적으로 전달할 수 있다고 판단했다”고 말했다. 현장을 찾은 관람객들은 스페이셜 사이니지가 구현한 캐릭터의 크기와 입체감에 주목했다. 콘텐츠 크리에이터 카와이 코코(Kawaii CoCo) 씨는 “캐릭터가 실제로 움직이며 상호작용하는 것처럼 생생하게 느껴졌다”며 “일반 디스플레이보다 훨씬 눈에 띄고 소셜미디어에서도 근사하게 보일 것 같아, 이 장면을 촬영해 제 구독자들에게 소개하고 싶다”고 말했다. ▲ 콘텐츠 크리에이터 카와이 코코 씨는 캐릭터의 움직임이 스페이셜 사이니지를 통해 생동감 있게 전달되어 아스트라에 오라티오 부스로 눈길이 갔다고 말했다. 스페이셜 사이니지는 52mm 1 의 얇은 두께에도 불구하고 마치 화면 뒤에 별도의 공간이 있는 듯한 깊이감을 구현한 것이 특징이다. 이러한 경험은 대중에게 게임과 캐릭터의 첫인상을 전달하는 데도 효과적으로 활용될 수 있다. 관람객 다니엘 아세로(Daniel Acero) 씨는 “처음 봤을 때 스크린 화면인 줄 전혀 몰랐고, 투명한 설치물이라고 생각했다”면서 “마치 화면 뒤에 실제 공간이 있는 것처럼 깊이감이 느껴져서 놀라웠고, 이러한 방식으로 게임 캐릭터를 소개하면 게임에 대한 관심을 높이고 캐릭터의 개성을 효과적으로 전달할 수 있을 것”이라고 말했다. 관람객 동선과 대기 공간에는 32형 스페이셜 사이니지가 설치돼 부스 전반으로 캐릭터 경험을 확장했다. 32형 제품은 49.4mm의 얇은 두께로 좁은 공간에도 유연하게 설치가 가능해, 게임 체험을 기다리는 관람객을 대상으로 캐릭터와 세계관에 대한 몰입도를 유지했다. 관람객 토마스 포르티에(Tomas NVIDIA is working to enable all nations to be AI nations — providing the technology, infrastructure, ecosystem and expertise needed to make this possible. To accelerate this transition across Southeast Asia, NVIDIA is helping nations move AI from experimentation to production-scale deployment through open models, developer tools and a broad partner ecosystem. Together, NVIDIA and its partners are focusing on four key areas: Enhancing government operations and service delivery. Developing accessible AI-powered citizen services, and empowering local businesses. Strengthening critical infrastructure and public safety. items.fullText: AI Security Is an Engineering Problem — How to Solve It at Every Layer of the Agent Stack Open research, controls across the agent stack and continuous testing help defenders build and operate more secure AI systems. September 21, 2026 by Saša Zdjelar 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! AI security is an engineering problem. That means defined security requirements, enforceable controls, named owners and evidence that protections work. As AI becomes more capable, the industry must accelerate security engineering, broaden access to defensive tools and share what works faster. Technology Changes, Security Fundamentals Endure The internet and cloud computing changed how software operates, while core security responsibilities endured: establish identity, control access, limit exposure and verify that protections work. AI agents introduce new capabilities — reasoning , using tools and adapting actions based on the data they encounter. Those capabilities require applying established principles to new operating conditions. This pace creates pressure. Organizations want the productivity benefits of AI while the practices to govern and secure these systems are still developing. Security Depends on the Full Agent Stack Applications depend on code, data, identities, services and infrastructure. Security depends on how those components work together — and AI agents extend that system . Models provide capabilities; harnesses organize context, tools and workflows; and runtime environments provide the infrastructure within which actions execute. Each part of that stack carries security responsibilities, and proper protection requires controls across each layer, as data, instructions and actions move through the system.
